To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the calf muscles differ significantly in their dynamic properties, (b) the muscles have similar 3D architecture, (c) passive components of the muscles are stretched and shortened by the muscle fibers, and (d) stretching of the passive components enhances the muscle force, whereas shortening depresses the force.

(1) maximum shortening velocity is about twice as high for gastrocnemii compared to soleus, (2) the force-velocity relation of gastrocnemii is more linear and less curved than the force-velocity relations of the other calf muscles, (3) enhancement effects are independent of ramp velocity, (4) depression effects are inversely related to ramp velocity, and (5) the depression effect is lowest for soleus.
The maximum shortening velocity of the calf muscles is highest for the gastrocnemii, intermediate for plantaris, and lowest for soleus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an experimental setup for the measurement of dynamic muscle properties and the three-dimensional architecture of muscles.
the dynamic and geometric properties of the gastrocnemicus (GAS), plantaris (PLA), soleus (SOL) and other shank muscles (FDL, EDL, TA).
the development of a muscle model that is able to simulate the dynamic behavior of a muscle in a realistic way.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

muscle architecture is not the main reason for the differences in the dynamic properties of the calf muscles, but rather that their different dynamic properties have evolved to meet the specific requirements of the muscle's function.
muscle parameters vary between different muscles, and even between individuals.
the soleus is a slow-twitch muscle, gastrocnemius a fast-twitch muscle, and the plantaris an intermediate one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the muscles of the rabbit shank show a large variation in their dynamic properties and architecture, which is not reflected in their force-length and force velocity relations.
the gastrocnemii (medial and lateral) have the highest dynamic properties and the highest muscle force production capacity, while the soleus has the lowest properties and force production.
the muscles of the rabbit calf are not only different in their architecture, but also show distinct differences in their dynamic behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
muscle parameters vary greatly among muscles, and that the muscle parameters should be determined individually.
the dynamic muscle parameters vary greatly among the muscles and that this variation has to be considered when using these muscles as actuators in simulations.
muscles differ in their dynamic properties and that the dynamic properties are not only dependent on the muscle architecture, but also depend on the muscle type.
